stories.title: Explore the Connected Door
stories.question: What does one entrance door require to function safely?
stories.summary: Follow D-101 through spaces, devices, systems, safety rules, suppliers, and maintainers.

steps.title: A door is never just a door
steps.body: Meet Main Entrance Door D-101. This story reveals the spaces, devices, systems, rules, suppliers, and people required for it to function safely.

steps.title: The spatial context
steps.body: D-101 serves the Main Lobby on Level 1 and sits on the public-to-secure boundary. The same object can be explored through spatial and system relationships.

steps.title: The devices that make it work
steps.body: Face recognition, card reader, electric lock, door contact, and camera each contribute a different relationship: authorize, secure, monitor, or report.

steps.title: Security must yield to life safety
steps.body: The fire alarm overrides the electric lock. The statutory Unlock on Fire Alarm rule explains why that cross-system dependency exists.

steps.title: Someone owns every relationship
steps.body: Security operates the access system, Facilities maintains the door and lock, and SecureVision supplies key devices. ONEXUS connects technical dependencies to accountable organizations.

steps.title: One object, one connected story
steps.body: ONEXUS shows that a door is connected to spaces, systems, rules, people, risks, and suppliers.

stories.title: Trace a Delivery Impact
stories.question: What happens when the face reader arrives three weeks late?
stories.summary: Trace a supplier signal into installation, testing, handover, cost exposure, ownership, and action.

steps.title: A supplier reports a three-week delay
steps.body: The face recognition reader will arrive on 25 September, twenty-one days later than planned. ONEXUS begins with the reported issue, not an abstract network.

steps.title: Trace the delayed item to the building
steps.body: The purchase order procures the reader, the reader controls D-101, and D-101 secures the lobby boundary. Procurement risk is now connected to a real building function.

steps.title: Follow the schedule blast radius
steps.body: Late delivery blocks installation. Installation precedes integrated testing, and testing gates the Level 1 security handover milestone. The activities have no usable float.

steps.title: Translate delay into commercial exposure
steps.body: Temporary access control, remobilisation, and extended preliminaries create an estimated ¥3.8–5.2M exposure. The estimate remains visibly marked as an estimate.

steps.title: Turn impact into a decision
steps.body: Project Controls must choose by 25 August: use a temporary reader or resequence the works. It is explicitly a required, not yet official decision.

steps.title: From supplier signal to accountable action
steps.body: One delay now has a traceable path through supplier, component, door, activities, milestone, cost, owner, and decision.

stories.title: Understand the Decision
stories.question: Why was face recognition recommended, and what does it affect?
stories.summary: Trace the question through evidence, alternatives, weighted criteria, recommendation, action, and outcome.

steps.title: Begin with the decision question
steps.body: The team must decide: how should entrance D-101 authenticate users? ONEXUS keeps the question connected to the project elements it will affect.

steps.title: Make the evidence traceable
steps.body: A verified security audit found tailgating, while the FM incident register recorded eighteen lost cards per quarter. The recommendation can be traced back to both sources.

steps.title: Preserve the alternatives
steps.body: The team considered card-only access, a mobile credential, and face recognition with card fallback. Rejected alternatives remain visible instead of disappearing from project memory.

steps.title: Show how the options were judged
steps.body: Security effectiveness carries 45%, privacy and acceptance 30%, and whole-life cost 25%. Each option retains its reviewed score against the relevant criteria.

steps.title: Reviewed does not mean official
steps.body: The reviewed recommendation selects face recognition with card fallback. Its record deliberately retains officialDecision: false until formal project approval occurs.

steps.title: Connect the decision to implementation and outcome
steps.body: The recommendation authorizes procurement, implements the face and card readers, affects D-101, and targets secure entry with a resilient fallback. The pending outcome can later validate—or challenge—the decision.
